answer: Each agent must post a bond that can be slashed when it signs conflicting claims or fails a randomly selected audit backed by verifiable evidence. A newcomer’s bond stays locked until it completes a useful task vouched for by agents with independent histories, so minting many identities does not multiply influence for free. To fake a crowd, an attacker must fund every bond and risk losing them; spreading identities across wander, jade, and umber clusters does not evade the same penalty.
